# Crimson Valley - a Blender recreation of a reference picture

`reference/reference.png` (1672 x 941): an alien valley at sunset - a banded gas giant and two moons,
a rock arch on the left, spires in mist, a winding river through red vegetation, waterfalls, and a
city on a second arch to the right. This folder rebuilds that picture as a real 3D scene in Blender
5.2 (geometry, procedural materials, lights, atmosphere), as close to the picture as it can be made.
The result is `crimson_valley.blend`; everything in it is generated by the scripts here.

## The idea

1. **Read the picture** (`tools/`, ordinary Python in `~/.cache/crimson_valley_tools/venv`): a depth
   model gives relative depth; the flat river is the ruler that turns it into metres
   (`calibrate.py`); masks say what is sky, valley floor, water, plants, mist. Result: `analysis/`.
2. **Make geometry from it** (`tools/build_meshes.py` -> `meshes/*.npz`): rock formations become closed
   solids whose camera-facing side follows the measured depth; the valley floor a terrain; the river a
   water plane.
3. **Build the scene in parts** (`scene/part_<name>.py` -> `parts/<name>.blend`), each alone and
   testable: sky, planet, moons, clouds, terrain, rocks, water, vegetation, city, waterfalls, mist,
   lighting, grade.
4. **Assemble** (`scene/assemble.py` -> `crimson_valley.blend`) and compare with the picture
   (`tools/compare.py`).

## Conventions (every script follows these)

- **World**: metres. X right, Y into the picture, Z up. The river's water is the plane z = 0. The camera
  is at (0, 0, 20), looks along +Y pitched 1.98 degrees down, 24 mm lens on a 36 mm sensor, 1672 x 941.
  `analysis/camera.json`; `tools/cvlib.py` (`Camera.unproject(u, v, depth)`, `.project(p)`, `.rays(u, v)`).
- **Picture coordinates**: (u, v) = pixels from the top-left corner, u right, v down; the pixel in row j,
  column i has its centre at (i + 0.5, j + 0.5). The horizon is the row v = 432.
- **Where things are**: say it in picture pixels and look the depth up (`analysis/depth.npy`: metres along
  the camera axis, 0 = sky), then `unproject` - never hard-coded world coordinates. If the calibration
  changes, a rebuild moves everything consistently.
- **Parts**: `scene/part_<name>.py` defines `build(col)` (create objects, link them into the collection
  `col`) and optionally `finalize(scene)` (runs in the assembled scene). A part never references another
  part's datablocks; shared data goes through files. Names start with `CV_`.
  The sky part makes the world `CV_World`; the grade part the compositor node group `CV_Compositing`.
- **Colour**: view transform **Standard**, exposure 0. So a surface that emits (r, g, b) in scene-linear
  shows as that colour: to show a reference pixel exactly, emit `common.srgb_to_linear(pixel)` at
  strength 1. Lit surfaces: albedo x light.
- **Honest 3D**: the reference picture is never mapped onto the scene as its colour. It may guide
  *layout*: masks (where plants, water, moss, cloud cover are) and measurements. Detail (rock texture,
  cloud wisps, leaves, ripples) is procedural or modelled.
- **Rendering**: Cycles on the GPU (OptiX). `common.render()` takes a file lock so parallel builds
  render one at a time. Previews: half size, 32-64 samples.

## Commands (`tools/cv`)

    tools/cv part <name> --render renders/<name>/a.png --scale 50 --samples 48 --with sky,rocks
    tools/cv assemble --render renders/full.png --scale 100 --samples 256
    tools/cv compare renders/full.png renders/full_cmp.png [--region x0 y0 x1 y1] [--mask sky|land|floor|water]
    tools/cv refcrop x0 y0 x1 y1 out.png --scale 3 --grid 50      # look at the reference up close
    tools/cv crop <render.png> x0 y0 x1 y1 out.png --to 1672x941 --scale 3 --grid 50
    tools/cv sam out_mask.png --points "x,y,1;x,y,0" --overlay out_overlay.png   # cut a mask out of the reference
    tools/cv py <script.py> ...                                  # analysis Python (isolated: -I)

## Rebuilding from nothing

    tools/cv py tools/depth_estimate.py reference/reference.png analysis/raw/depth_dav2s.npy depth-anything/Depth-Anything-V2-Small-hf 1218
    tools/cv py tools/depth_estimate.py reference/reference.png analysis/raw/depth_dav1l.npy LiheYoung/depth-anything-large-hf 1218
    tools/cv py tools/analyze.py analysis/raw --water analysis/raw/water_sam.png
    tools/cv py tools/build_meshes.py
    for p in sky planet moons clouds terrain rocks water vegetation city waterfalls mist lighting grade; do tools/cv part $p; done
    tools/cv assemble --render renders/full.png

`renders/` holds previews and comparisons only (safe to delete).
